title: Weightlifting: clean and jerk
rulebook: IWF Technical and Competition Rules & Regulations (International Weightlifting Federation; 2020 edition, article numbers quoted from memory of the 2020s editions): 2.3 the clean and jerk, 2.5 incorrect movements, 3.1 the platform, 3.3 the barbell (the women's bar: 15 kg, 2.01 m, a 25 mm grip section 1.31 m long, sleeves 50 mm thick; collars 2.5 kg; the lightest barbell in competition, women: 21 kg = the bar, two collars and two 0.5 kg discs)
deviations: 3.3 (the barbell): the barbell is an aluminium technique bar, American Barbell's ATB-5-E (5 kg, 1.835 m, a 25 mm grip section 1.31 m long as the women's bar's, sleeves 50 mm thick), training equipment, not a competition barbell (the women's bar is 15 kg, the lightest competition barbell 21.0 kg), without collars or discs. The reason is the robot's arms: with the women's 15 kg bar the turnover from the hang to the shoulders asks 1.08 to 1.17 times what the elbow and shoulder motors give, and with 10 kg the robot topples at the turnover, so neither a heavier bar nor a faster turnover is open. There is no choice of weight and no progression of attempts, because the task is one attempt

3.1 and 3.3 (the bar on the platform, on its discs): the bar rests by its sleeves on two lifting blocks 0.35 m high (a block clean & jerk, a standard training form), so that its axis is 0.375 m above the platform; a competition bar on its 0.45 m discs lies at 0.225 m, but the squat to that height is out of the robot's reach: its hips would have to flex past where the hip links meet the pelvis (the robot's own body collides with itself), and every squat tried fell back onto a thigh. Without discs or blocks the bar would lie on its inner collars 0.04 m above the platform, where the hands' curled fingers cannot close round it without touching the platform

3.3 (what the maker does not give): the bar's 5.0 kg are split 1.74 kg for the shaft and the rest between the two revolving sleeves with their inner collars (0.08 m across, 0.03 m wide); these are estimates

3.3 (the grip): each hand is the H1-2's own Inspire five-finger hand (six self-locking drives; 20 N at each fingertip, 30 N at the thumb), open at the start; it holds the bar by its fingers' and palm's contact and friction alone (nothing is welded; no chalk, no hook grip with the thumb under the fingers), and the bar can slip, turn in the hand and drop. A hand holds the bar while the grip section touches that hand's fingers (closed round it; a break of up to 0.05 s, the contact flickering under a load, is not letting go)

2.3.1 (the clean): the referee judges the end of the clean, not the movement: the bar at the shoulders (its axis within 0.15 m of both shoulder joints; the robot's rigid chest stands 0.07 m ahead of them, so the bar cannot lie on the collarbones) with the legs extended, the feet on one line and everything motionless for 0.5 s (the rule says "motionless" and gives no time); that the bar came there in a single movement is not judged, because that needs a human reading of the pull

the rules' "at the shoulders" and "overhead" assume a lifter who stands under the bar; so that neither position can be reached bent over or with the bar behind the back, in both the trunk must be upright (the cosine of its tilt at least 0.94), the bar's centre no more than 0.25 m (horizontally) from the point midway between the shoulder joints, and the bar within 20.0 degrees of the line through the shoulder joints (seen from above)

2.5 (incorrect movements): judged here are the unfinished attempt above knee height, a part other than the feet on the platform, leaving the platform, the incomplete extension of the arms and legs at the finish and the feet not on one line; not judged, because they need a human judge's reading of the movement: the press-out and a pause while the arms extend, pulling from the hang, the bar touching the thighs, the elbows or upper arms touching the knees or thighs, an uneven extension of the arms, the oscillation of the bar before the jerk

2.3.2 (the finish): "fully extended" is read from the robot's joints: each elbow within 10.0 degrees and each knee within 10.0 degrees of straight; "motionless" is the bar and the pelvis slower than 0.1 m/s; the three referees' "down" signal is given by the simulator when the final position has been held for 2.0 s, and the attempt ends there: lowering the bar after the signal is not part of the task

6.6 (the clock): the athlete's one minute runs here from the start of the episode to the down signal (60 s for the whole attempt); the rule's minute runs from the call to the platform to the start of the lift, and there is no call here

texts.sentence: Clean and jerk the barbell: lift it from its blocks to your shoulders, then to locked arms overhead, and hold it there motionless until the down signal.
texts.rules: The barbell is an aluminium technique bar (5.0 kg, 1.835 m long; the grip section between the inner collars is 1.31 m long and 0.025 m thick; the sleeves are 0.2325 m long and 0.05 m thick and revolve on the bar), without discs or collars: 5.0 kg. It rests by its sleeves on two lifting blocks (0.35 m high) standing on the competition platform (4.0 m by 4.0 m, 0.1 m high), on which you stand. Your hands are five-finger hands, open at the start; a hand holds the bar while the bar's grip section touches that hand's fingers (a break of up to 0.05 s is not letting go); they hold it by contact and friction only, so it can slip, turn in the hands and drop. Lift-off: the bar may leave its blocks only in both hands: you fail the moment the bar's axis is more than 0.03 m above where it lies at rest while fewer than two hands hold it. The attempt: once the bar's centre has been 0.48 m above the platform (knee height) the lift must be finished: from then on you fail if either hand lets go or if any part of the barbell touches the platform or a block before the down signal. The clean: the bar must first rest at your shoulders: its axis within 0.15 m of both shoulder joints, both hands on it, both knees within 10.0 degrees of straight, both feet on the platform and on one line, the bar and your pelvis slower than 0.1 m/s, and you under the bar (your trunk upright: the cosine of its tilt at least 0.94; the bar's centre no more than 0.25 m, horizontally, from the point midway between your shoulder joints; the bar, seen from above, within 20.0 degrees of the line through them), with the attempt begun (the bar has been above knee height and touches nothing but you), all of it without a break for 0.5 s. You fail if the bar's axis is more than 0.25 m above the centre of your head before that (a lift from the platform to overhead in one movement is a snatch). The jerk and the finish: after the clean, bring the bar overhead. The final position is: the bar's axis at least 0.25 m above the centre of your head, both hands on it, both elbows within 10.0 degrees of straight (the angle between the upper arm's and the forearm's long axes), both knees within 10.0 degrees of straight (the angle hip, knee, ankle), both feet on the platform and on one line (their centres no more than 0.05 m apart along the horizontal direction square to the bar; under a bar tilted more than 60.0 degrees from level the feet never count as on one line), the bar and your pelvis slower than 0.1 m/s, and you under the bar as in the clean (trunk upright, the bar's centre over the middle of your shoulders, the bar along your shoulder line). Once it is held for 2.0 s without a break the down signal is given: that is success, and the attempt ends. At any time you fail if a part of you other than your feet touches the platform, if any part of you touches a block, if any part of you or of the barbell touches the floor beside the platform, or after 60 s. There is no other fall rule: you may squat as low as you like, and the bar may touch your body.
texts.venue: You stand upright in the middle of the platform, facing +x, your soles 0.1 m above the floor, in the rest pose (upper arms down, forearms forward). The barbell lies across your front, parallel to your shoulders and centred on you, its sleeves on two blocks (0.30 m along x, 0.20 m along y, 0.35 m high, centred 0.8 m to either side of you): its axis is 0.2 m ahead of your pelvis and 0.375 m above the platform, just beyond your toes (they reach 0.164 m ahead of your pelvis). Your shoulder joints are 1.46 m above the platform when you stand, 0.30 m apart; the centre of your head is at 1.70 m, its top at 1.79 m; your knee joints are at 0.48 m. In the `stand` action's stance your knees are bent by about 21 degrees, and your elbows are at a right angle in the rest pose: neither is extended. Your elbow joints have no stop at the straight arm (they bend both ways from it). Both hands are open (grip values 0): a grip value is that hand's closure command (0 open, the fingers straight; 1 every finger and the thumb closing; a finger stops on what it touches). The barbell is a free body: `held` in your state says which hand grasps it with its fingers and its thumb or palm. The platform's edges are 2 m away in every direction.
texts.difficulty: The bar is light, but the hands hold it only by their fingers' friction. Turning it over from the hang to the shoulders, slowly, asks about half of what the elbow and shoulder motors give; too fast, and the bar slides out of the hands. Nothing balances the robot under a load, and no built-in action bends down to the bar or straightens the knees.

stand.meaning: the platform holds the legs in the stance; you give the waist's 1 and the arms' 14 joint targets (rad) (grip_left: the left hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch); grip_right: the right hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch))

walk.meaning: Unitree's walking policy drives the legs from the velocity command (vx forward, vy to the left, m/s; wz turning left, rad/s; the robot's own frame); you give the waist and arm joint targets (grip_left: the left hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch); grip_right: the right hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch))

joints.meaning: you give all 27 joint targets (rad); the default PD gains, no feed-forward (grip_left: the left hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch); grip_right: the right hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch))

lowcmd.meaning: Unitree's LowCmd for all 27 joints: position targets (rad), velocity targets (rad/s), feed-forward torques (N m), kp, kd; the motor torque is kp (q - q_measured) + kd (dq - dq_measured) + tau, evaluated at 1 kHz (grip_left: the left hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch); grip_right: the right hand's closure command, 0 (open, the fingers straight) to 1 (every drive closing towards its closed position; fingers stop on what they touch))

robot.name: unitree_h1
robot.title: Unitree H1-2
robot.model: Unitree H1-2, 27 joints, 1.78 m, 67 kg (RoboOlympics robot library h1-4: the H1-2 body (Unitree's own h1_2 model, its joint ranges and speed limits) with Unitree H2 / H2-X-class leg actuators from the H2's official URDF (hips and knees 360 N m, ankle pitch 66.88 N m; curves of Unitree's M107 shape, 2.5 kW peak per joint) and H2-class arm actuators from the same URDF (shoulder pitch 130 N m; shoulder roll and yaw, elbow, forearm roll 60 N m; curves of Unitree's N7520 / N5020 shapes); the H1-2's own torso (M107-15, 200 N m), ankle roll and wrist pitch / yaw (estimates))

left.model: the H1-2's Inspire RH56DFX five-finger hand (6 self-locking linear drives for 12 joints: the thumb's rotation and flexion, one drive per finger with its two joints coupled; Unitree's H1-2 kinematics) with H2-class fingertip forces: 20 N per finger and 30 N the thumb, 2 x the RH56DFX's 10 / 15 N (Unitree's H2 Plus offers 20 N Sharpa Wave hands; Inspire's RH56E2 gives 28 / 30 N)

servo.rule: each drive: a setpoint moves towards open + closure x (closed - open) at most speed_rad_s, but closing stops where kp (setpoint - q) would exceed active_torque_nm; torque = clip(kp (setpoint - q) + kd (setpoint speed - dq), -passive, passive) at every physics step; a load beyond passive_torque_nm drags the setpoint (the drive slips)

left.holding_rule: a free body that touches the hand's fingers and its thumb or palm

right.model: the H1-2's Inspire RH56DFX five-finger hand (6 self-locking linear drives for 12 joints: the thumb's rotation and flexion, one drive per finger with its two joints coupled; Unitree's H1-2 kinematics) with H2-class fingertip forces: 20 N per finger and 30 N the thumb, 2 x the RH56DFX's 10 / 15 N (Unitree's H2 Plus offers 20 N Sharpa Wave hands; Inspire's RH56E2 gives 28 / 30 N)

servo.rule: each drive: a setpoint moves towards open + closure x (closed - open) at most speed_rad_s, but closing stops where kp (setpoint - q) would exceed active_torque_nm; torque = clip(kp (setpoint - q) + kd (setpoint speed - dq), -passive, passive) at every physics step; a load beyond passive_torque_nm drags the setpoint (the drive slips)

right.holding_rule: a free body that touches the hand's fingers and its thumb or palm
